preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained ownership)
Contract must have ETH balance (from accumulated fees or direct transfers)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setOperationsAddress() to set the operations address to a malicious contract you control. Then trigger swapBack() (via trading or forceSwapBack()) to make the contract send its ETH balance to your malicious address via the low-level call at line 563. The malicious contract should have a fallback/receive function that captures the ETH.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The FoundationToken contract has a critical vulnerability in the swapBack() function. At line 563 (in the original code), the contract performs (success,) = address(operationsAddress).call{value: address(this).balance}(""); This sends ALL remaining ETH balance to the operationsAddress. The operationsAddress can be changed by the owner via setOperationsAddress(). As the attacker, if we can become the owner, we can set operationsAddress to a malicious contract we control, then trigger swapBack() to drain all ETH from the contract.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner (or impersonate the owner). 2. Deploy a malicious contract with a receive() function to capture ETH. 3. Call setOperationsAddress() to point to our malicious contract. 4. Ensure the contract has ETH balance (send some ETH to it). 5. Trigger swapBack() via forceSwapBack() (requires sufficient token balance) or by creating a trade that triggers the automatic swap. 6. The ETH will be sent to our malicious contract, which we can then withdraw.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the current owner (we need to find who the owner is first). 2. Deploy a simple MaliciousReceiver contract with receive() function. 3. Call setOperationsAddress() on the target contract to set it to our MaliciousReceiver. 4. Send some ETH to the target contract (using deal() or direct transfer). 5. Since forceSwapBack() requires the contract to have token balance >= swapTokensAtAmount, we need to either: a) Transfer tokens to the contract to meet the threshold, or b) Enable trading and create a trade that generates fees. 6. Call forceSwapBack() to trigger the ETH transfer to our malicious address. 7. Withdraw ETH from the malicious contract to the attacker.
